classifier_causes.cause: Policy detection searches heading plus body for finance/agreement/responsibility nouns, causing semantic leakage into technical controls, captions, advice and navigation. Link-label text also contaminates policy detection. Exact exceptions grow without a semantic category contract.
Security best practice is explicitly forced into owner confirmation even though the text does not say platform enforcement or obligation.

Source lane asks an owner to supply canonical code already available; owner lane requires a new dated decision; citation lane asks owner for source. Existing authoritative publication is not modeled as an alternative, and account meaning is conflated with policy authority.

Independent current-delta classifier is limited to specific tax words on one page and SSH special case, while historical classifier is broad. This creates history-dependent lane assignments and drops surrounding list qualifiers in new blocks. Actual no-withholding claim falls through because regex tax is singular.
Source and owner demands are merged into the same owner register, making a missing implementation locator look like a Product/Finance/Legal approval block.

correction_strategy: Preserve frozen records; add exact ID, text/span/page hash-bound reviewed taxonomy dispositions. No generic keyword removal or page-wide PASS.

Use one semantic classifier for historical and current delta paths. Distinguish publication/contract meaning; implemented state; declared interface; UI; recommendation; illustration; navigation; editorial lead-in. Headings supply context but never manufacture a claim absent from the actual row.
Retain true logical list preambles, but do not propagate policy words from unrelated headings or link labels. Reconcile full current production inventory rather than validating only toy strings.

For genuine policy/financial/tax claims, make exact applicable authoritative source an accepted basis; accountable human decision is an alternative or escalation for missing/ambiguous/conflicting authority, not a second mandatory approval for published terms.

Use independent source-origin and exact support checks for authority. Retained docs summaries, registry records, graph paths and authored rationale cannot become terminal product proof. A classification correction never implies PASS.

Separate operator/runtime prerequisites from engineering-source retrieval and genuine decision-needed rows. Mark unavailable only from an actual failed source/access search; missing proof alone remains UNVALIDATED.

Add parity regressions on every selected real occurrence and a all-owner census test. Keep negative tests for genuine minimum payout, contract lock-in, tax withholding, support disclaimers and datacenter requirements. Verify false owner removal does not erase their real authority/source/runtime needs.
critical_exception_rules: A recommendation to enable 2FA or scope/rotate API keys is operational advice. An assertion that a role requires 2FA or a key permits registration is an actual enforcement/capability claim requiring source and representative evidence; neither means automatic Legal approval.

Agreement acceptance as a UI/account state is technical. Statements that the agreement creates obligations, locks terms, disclaims liability, or allocates support responsibility need exact governing authority.

Price option names, units, hypothetical examples, pricing advice and navigation labels do not set commercial terms. Existing-rental price persistence, fees, payout minimum/timing, accepted rate and actual revenue accrual remain authoritative financial/contract claims.

Payout/invoice screen labels, export actions, team context and invoice fields are technical/UI. Paid and Pending assertions need backend event mapping, not just a screenshot. A $20 minimum, Friday schedule or disclaimed provider liability remains a financial rule.

Bare technical contract IDs/events are not legal terms; complete lead-ins such as While a rental contract is active must still be applied when their list items state duties. Do not erase true obligations while removing heading leakage.

Support/dedicated-account claims may mix best practice with an assertion that a setup is unsupported. Preserve and separately source the asserted support boundary; do not call the whole mixed paragraph editorial.

The full Terms/applicable agreement source must support exact mining, export, private-data and noninterference language. An agreement ban on reading data does not automatically prove a ban on stopping containers or copying logs; retain unsatisfied subsets.

Source-first is not owner-free in every future case. Owner escalation remains correct for an actual unavailable governing source, contradiction, new policy choice, or unresolved applicability judgment, but this audit did not establish any owner unavailable merely because evidence is missing.

records.title: Hosting Overview
records.text:
As a host, you are responsible for:
- Keeping rented machines online, stable, and dedicated to renter workloads.

context.text: Vast is a GPU marketplace. Hosts provide machines; renters run workloads on them.
As a host, you are responsible for:
- Installing and maintaining Ubuntu, NVIDIA drivers, storage, networking, and the Vast host software.
- Keeping rented machines online, stable, and dedicated to renter workloads.
- Setting prices, offer end dates, and maintenance windows.

- Troubleshooting local hardware problems. [Hosting Agreement — Performance of Services](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement) assigns the provider responsibility for running, troubleshooting, and maintaining the hardware.
- Troubleshooting local driver, storage, and network problems.

context.text: <span id="separate-host-account" aria-hidden="true" />
## Do I need a separate host account?

Yes. Use a dedicated account for hosting. Do not use the same account for both client rentals and host operations, because that setup is unsupported and can cause account and machine-management issues.
If a business or fleet needs multiple operators, use a dedicated host team account instead of sharing one personal login. See [Host Teams](/host/host-teams).

records.title: Host Account and Agreement
headings: What if I accepted the agreement but still see a client account?
records.text: Confirm that you are signed into the correct dedicated host account, then refresh or sign out and back in. If the Machines tab is still missing, treat it as an account-state issue rather than a Linux install issue. Contact Vast support with the host account email and screenshots or error messages from the setup flow.

context.text: <span id="agreement-stuck" aria-hidden="true" />
## What if I accepted the agreement but still see a client account?

Confirm that you are signed into the correct dedicated host account, then refresh or sign out and back in. If the Machines tab is still missing, treat it as an account-state issue rather than a Linux install issue. Contact Vast support with the host account email and screenshots or error messages from the setup flow.

context.text: ## Setup Path

5. **List the machine.** Set your price and terms with [Pricing Your Listing](/host/pricing-your-listing).

context.text: 1. **Truncated or mangled setup key.** Always copy the full command with the setup page's copy button; a partial paste fails authentication. Get a fresh command and rerun.
2. **Expired setup key.** Setup commands are single-use and expire. Refresh the setup page and copy a fresh command — do not rerun an old one from shell history.
3. **Account not converted to a host account.** The API rejects machines from client-only accounts. See [Host Account and Agreement](/host/account-hosting-agreement#agreement-stuck).
4. **Stale installer or retired endpoint.** An old downloaded installer can call endpoints that no longer exist. Re-download the installer from the setup page instead of reusing a cached copy.
If the log shows a local driver, Docker, or cgroup error rather than an API 4xx, use the general causes above and [Host Diagnostics](/host/common-errors-diagnostics#logs).

context.text: ## Step 12: List, Self-Test, And Monitor
1. List the machine and set pricing.

2. Run the self-test from any machine with the CLI: [How to Self-Test](/host/how-to-self-test). If the installer starts the self-test automatically, it may wait about 10 minutes for the daemon to initialize; watch `/var/lib/vastai_kaalia/self_test.log`.

4. Watch the first day over SSH: keep an eye on `vastai.service`, Docker, GPU visibility, port reachability, and the self-test log.

records.title: Volume Offers
records.text: 1. **Prepare host storage.** Put Docker's data root on fast SSD or NVMe storage using XFS project quotas. See [Storage Setup](/host/storage-setup).

context.text: ## Volume Lifecycle
1. **Prepare host storage.** Put Docker's data root on fast SSD or NVMe storage using XFS project quotas. See [Storage Setup](/host/storage-setup).
2. **Publish a volume offer.** Create it with the machine listing or list storage separately. This advertises a maximum rentable capacity; it does not create a renter volume.
3. **A renter creates a volume.** The renter searches offers and chooses a fixed size. That allocation persists independently of any one instance.
4. **The renter attaches it to an instance.** A new or existing volume is linked while a Docker instance is created and appears at the selected mount path.

records.text: For example, if you advertise a 500 GB offer and a renter creates a 200 GB volume, include that 200 GB allocation in your storage plan. Keep enough headroom for active volume contracts and new instance creation.

context.text: The capacity in a volume offer is the maximum amount renters may allocate; publishing the offer does not itself create a renter volume. When a renter creates a volume, its requested size is allocated from that offer and must be included when you plan the shared disk pool.

For example, if you advertise a 500 GB offer and a renter creates a 200 GB volume, include that 200 GB allocation in your storage plan. Keep enough headroom for active volume contracts and new instance creation.
<Warning>

Do not remove renter files or edit Docker's storage directories manually to reclaim space. Use the normal offer, instance, and volume lifecycle. If the platform's available-capacity figures do not reconcile, collect the machine and offer output before contacting support.

context.text: ## Interruptible Minimum Bid
The minimum bid is a floor, not your expected on-demand price. Set it near the lowest price you are willing to accept, often close to loaded power cost.

If the floor is too high, GPUs may sit idle. If it is too low, interruptible work may not cover operating cost. Do not set the floor close to the on-demand price just because that is the price you hope to receive.

records.title: Why Isn't My Machine in Search?
headings: Listed and visible are different things
records.text: Separate "listed" from "visible in a normal broad search." Marketplace search is not a complete inventory dump. It limits result sets, ranks and groups similar offers, tries to avoid race conditions, and usually shows the best matches first. Search can be affected by ranking, grouping, filters, verification state, offer state, rental state, reliability, price, supply and demand, or machine errors.

context.text: ## Listed and visible are different things

Separate "listed" from "visible in a normal broad search." Marketplace search is not a complete inventory dump. It limits result sets, ranks and groups similar offers, tries to avoid race conditions, and usually shows the best matches first. Search can be affected by ranking, grouping, filters, verification state, offer state, rental state, reliability, price, supply and demand, or machine errors.

records.title: Reliability & Uptime
headings: Why does reliability drop after rentals, reboots, or disconnects?
records.text: If you must take the machine offline, minimize the offline time. The score also takes the machine's average earnings into account: machines with lower earnings are penalized less for offline time.

context.text: Reliability can drop when the platform observes instability, failed starts, disconnections, downtime, network failures, driver or GPU failures, thermal or power events, or active rental disruption. Short rentals can expose startup and runtime failures quickly. Reboots or disconnects during active commitments can hurt reliability.
If you must take the machine offline, minimize the offline time. The score also takes the machine's average earnings into account: machines with lower earnings are penalized less for offline time.

headings: Will restarting lower reliability or remove verification?
records.text: Reliability does not directly determine verification state by itself. Plan restarts around active contracts and use maintenance windows whenever possible.

Reliability does not directly determine verification state by itself. Verification is separate from the reliability score, but outages, failed starts, driver issues, network drops, or other instability can reduce reliability and may eventually contribute to deverification if the machine becomes unhealthy. Plan restarts around active contracts and use maintenance windows whenever possible.

records.title: Removing or Recreating Machines
headings: How do I unlist, delete, or recreate a machine?
records.text: Unlisting stops new rental contracts from being created, but it does not end existing contracts. Deleting or recreating a machine should only happen after active commitments and stored workloads are understood. Recreating may be useful after a failed install, stale record, or major hardware change, but do not use undocumented reset or recovery flags unless Vast support specifically instructs you to do so.

context.text: <span id="unlist-delete-recreate" aria-hidden="true" />
## How do I unlist, delete, or recreate a machine?

Unlisting stops new rental contracts from being created, but it does not end existing contracts. Deleting or recreating a machine should only happen after active commitments and stored workloads are understood. Recreating may be useful after a failed install, stale record, or major hardware change, but do not use undocumented reset or recovery flags unless Vast support specifically instructs you to do so.
From the CLI, see [vastai unlist machine](/cli/reference/unlist-machine), [vastai delete machine](/cli/reference/delete-machine), and [vastai cleanup machine](/cli/reference/cleanup-machine).

headings: What changes when I swap GPUs or other hardware?
records.text: Hardware changes can affect verification, search visibility, offers, and client expectations. Reducing GPU count, RAM, disk, or advertised capacity can trigger deverification or contract problems. Adding or replacing GPUs may require the host daemon or backend to refresh machine specs, and you may need to rerun self-test. The same-GPU-type guideline still applies; see [Supported Hardware](/host/supported-hardware).

headings: What should I do with a ghost machine?
records.text: First inspect whether the machine has active contracts, stored instances or volumes, visible offers, or backend state preventing deletion. Use the normal unlist/delete/cleanup path only when safe. If a stale backend record remains after normal cleanup, collect the account context, screenshots or CLI output, and relevant logs, then contact Vast support.

## What should I do with a ghost machine?

First inspect whether the machine has active contracts, stored instances or volumes, visible offers, or backend state preventing deletion. Use the normal unlist/delete/cleanup path only when safe. If a stale backend record remains after normal cleanup, collect the account context, screenshots or CLI output, and relevant logs, then contact Vast support.

context.text: ## Invoice Information

## Escalate To Vast Support
Escalate account conversion, hosting agreement, payout, API permission, backend machine record, ghost machine, suspected backend bug, or platform-state mismatch issues.

context.text: <span id="generic-red-machine-error" aria-hidden="true" />
## Generic Red Machine Error

A red machine error means the host software or platform detected a machine-health, network, storage, driver, container, VM, or policy issue. Fix the specific cause first, then allow the platform to refresh.

If the host looks healthy but the console state remains wrong, collect logs and escalate to Vast support. Do not assume support can manually verify ordinary machines; verification and most eligibility checks are automated.

context.text: ## Host Responsibilities
While a rental contract is active:
- Keep the advertised machine online, stable, and performant.
- Do not run local gaming, mining, benchmarks, display workloads, or background GPU jobs.
- Do not stop, inspect, modify, or interfere with renter containers because they appear idle.
- Keep renter data isolated.
- Keep escalation contact details current in [Settings](https://cloud.vast.ai/settings/) so Vast can reach the right responder for urgent hosted-machine issues.
- Follow the host agreement, terms, export rules, and applicable law.

context.text: ## Host Responsibilities
While a rental contract is active:
- Keep the advertised machine online, stable, and performant.
- Do not run local gaming, mining, benchmarks, display workloads, or background GPU jobs.
- Do not stop, inspect, modify, or interfere with renter containers because they appear idle.
- Keep renter data isolated.
- Keep escalation contact details current in [Settings](https://cloud.vast.ai/settings/) so Vast can reach the right responder for urgent hosted-machine issues.
- Follow the host agreement, terms, export rules, and applicable law.

context.text: ## What you commit to, in plain language
Under the [Hosting Agreement](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement), listing a machine creates offers that clients can accept as rental contracts. For each active rental contract, you commit to:
- Provide the hardware and services according to all the advertised specs.
- Not use the hardware for any other purpose while it is rented.
- Keep the client's data isolated and protected according to the data protection policy.

- Use reasonable safeguards and physical security around the hardware to protect Vast.ai Content. See [Hosting Agreement — Intellectual Property and Data Security](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement).
- Provide the advertised services until each rental contract's rental end date.

Under the [Hosting Agreement](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement), listing a machine creates offers that clients can accept as rental contracts. For each active rental contract, you commit to:
- Not use the hardware for any other purpose while it is rented.

context.text: ## What you commit to, in plain language
Under the [Hosting Agreement](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement), listing a machine creates offers that clients can accept as rental contracts. For each active rental contract, you commit to:
- Provide the hardware and services according to all the advertised specs.
- Not use the hardware for any other purpose while it is rented.
- Keep the client's data isolated and protected according to the data protection policy.

- Use reasonable safeguards and physical security around the hardware to protect Vast.ai Content. See [Hosting Agreement — Intellectual Property and Data Security](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/agreement).
- Provide the advertised services until each rental contract's rental end date.
